Some kid at Costco left this game running on one of the iMacs back in 2017. "Hey, that looks like a cool game," I thought, memorising the link of the website and opening it on my own computer back then. Played for about a month, then eventually grew bored after "hacking" the game with the browser console.

Fast forward 9 years, I'm dealing with lots of stuff in life. I wished how things would go back to the good old days... and there it was. The old memory of that one clicker game. Cookie clicker. I decide to buy the game on Steam, grab a few workshop mods while I'm at it, and there it is. The game to take my mind off stress, or to leave running while I'm doing something else. 

Damn, who knew clicking cookies would be so addicting?

As much as I like Cookie Clicker, I unfortunately have to give it a negative review.

I have played far more than my Steam playtime suggests, including the browser version, the mobile version and the Switch version. Cookie Clicker is undeniably one of the most important idle games ever made. It basically created or at least massively shaped the entire idle/clicker genre, and very few games have been as influential.

However, when you compare Cookie Clicker to modern idle game standards, I honestly do not think it holds up that well anymore.

Everything before the first Ascension is great. You make steady progress, unlock lots of fun achievements like True Neverclick, Hardcore or selling a grandma, and the game constantly feels fresh and creative. Clicking a Golden Cookie feels exciting because it gives you a meaningful boost, and pulling off your first combos is genuinely fun.

But this

There is no game here in any traditional sense. You click a cookie. You buy things that click the cookie for you. You ascend and do it again with multipliers.
